evidence.quote: Novartis’ experimental cardiovascular drug fails a pivotal study.
A closely watched cardiovascular drug from Novartis failed in a pivotal study, the company said Friday, a major blow to the firm and to efforts to target a common heart disease risk factor.

The drug, called pelacarsen, had shown in earlier trials that it could drastically lower levels of what’s called Lp(a), a little blob of lipids and proteins that at elevated concentrations increases the likelihood of severe heart problems.
But Novartis said that in the Phase 3 HORIZON trial, pelacarsen failed to reduce the risk of cardiovascular death or emergencies like heart attacks or stroke compared to placebo.

Here the authors show that aging oocytes leak mitochondrial DNA into the cytosol where it activates the cGAS-STING pathway, driving inflammatory signaling in oocytes as well as neighboring granulosa cells via cGAMP transfer.
Inhibiting this pathway ameliorates ovarian aging.

results.verbatim: Results: The rainfall-case association peaked at a 1-month lag (r = 0.551; 95 % CI 0.437-0.647; p < 0.001) and remained significant through 3 months.

bc76a602df47ffef.title: Altered oligodendrocyte function promotes cognitive decline in aging
digest: Leveraging a human brain tissue bank with cognitive data across the lifespan, we identify a role for oligodendrocytes — myelin-producing cells in the brain — in age-related cognitive decline.

With worsening cognitive decline, oligodendrocytes become dysfunctional and produce myelin of poor integrity, and experimental modeling of this myelin pathology impairs cognitive performance in aging.

44f4a5ba817ee4da.title: Blood cells replace the immune cells of the ageing human brain
digest: At birth, the brain contains its own immune cells, called microglia, that are thought to persist throughout life without being replaced by cells from outside the brain.

Studies that trace cell lineage now show that these cells are replaced by circulating immune cells during ageing, revealing a previously unappreciated interaction between the brain and the rest of the body.
